title: Downtown parking strategy received; 2024 plan approved
subtitle: Bridge replacements, bio-resin road base contract, CommunityConnect grant pilot, and a request to bore a fertilizer pipe under roads.
overview: Council received the Municipal Downtown Parking Strategy for information only and approved the 2024 implementation plan {{vote:m3}}. Paid parking is not being introduced this year. Staff will investigate paid and permit parking, continue the shuttle and timed-parking enforcement, add accessible and 15-minute spaces, and report back during 2025 budget planning. Staff will also look at running enforcement outside the County process.

Council endorsed replacing three bridges in the northwest of the township and removing two without replacement, ending a long-running closure problem for farm, emergency and local traffic {{vote:m4}}. It also approved a single-source contract for bio-resin road base stabilization on Eighth Line, following a 2023 trial segment {{vote:m5}}.

Council approved a pilot CommunityConnect program, replacing the Neighbourhood Grant Program, with a 2024 budget of $8,300 {{vote:m7}}. A farm-business delegate asked to bore a pipe under two roads to pump fertilizer, and the request was referred to Infrastructure Services staff for a report {{vote:m1}}.

decisions.detail: Council received the strategy for information, directed staff to carry out the 2024 implementation plan, and delegated contract signing authority for 2024 implementation to the Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer.
Staff will investigate administering parking enforcement outside the County process and report back, and will bring the strategy back for adoption with the 2025 budget process.
Council endorsed replacing Bridges 28-P, 32-P and 33-P, removing Bridges 1-P and 30-P without replacement, and publishing the Notice of Study Completion.
Council approved a single-source contract with BioDiffusion Technologies Inc. for bio-resin road base stabilization, with an upset limit of $191,868 including non-rebate HST.
Council approved the 2024 pilot, renamed the Neighbourhood Grant Program as CommunityConnect, and raised its budget to $8,300.
Council referred a request to bore a 6-inch pipe under Eighth Line West and Middlebrook Road to Infrastructure Services staff for a report back.

debate: On parking, several councillors said they were comfortable receiving the report for information but not approving it, and had concerns about 2025 items such as paid parking and permits. One councillor said parking passes priced out of reach for some residents would not be equitable.

Councillors asked that Fergus and Elora be treated differently on paid parking, since Fergus downtown serves more local errands. They also asked for consultation with the BIAs and the public before anything beyond 2024 comes forward. Staff said consultation would happen.

Staff said 2024 enforcement would stay close to the 2023 level, because paid parking is the main revenue source and there is no money for more. One councillor asked whether more enforcement would pay for itself. One councillor questioned paving the Bissell Park east lot because of its closeness to the river and salt loading. The consultant said that recommendation needs more study.

On the pipeline request, councillors asked about water supply risk, conservation authority involvement and whether other municipalities allow it. The delegate said it would cut tractor trips, noise, road wear and accident risk. Staff were asked to look at the question more broadly in case similar requests follow.

On the bio-resin trial, councillors asked what the product is, whether it reduces potholes, and how it compares in cost with conventional methods. The company said it strengthened the base by about 20% in the trial. Staff said it could extend pavement life.
